runtime\u003c/strong\u003e designed for AI agents. You write structured markdown files containing polyglot code blocks — mixing C, Python, Rust, or any language line by line — and the FLUX compiler weaves them into a single optimized, verifiable bytecode that runs on a 64-register Micro-VM.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBut that's the mechanics. Here's the \u003cstrong\u003eidea\u003c/strong\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFLUX-ese is what you get when you make a programming language that reads like a lawyer writes a contract. Every word is defined. Every operation is precise. Custom definitions are spelled out up front, like \"for the purposes of this operation, 'depth' means sonar reading in fathoms corrected for tidal state.\" The language is \u003cstrong\u003enatural but precise\u003c/strong\u003e — like legalese is to lawyers, FLUX-ese is to agents.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe key insight: if a translator can turn any line of code in any language into a line of FLUX-ese, then you have a \u003cstrong\u003ecommon language\u003c/strong\u003e that's completely observable, understandable, and changeable by humans — both technical and non-technical. You don't need to read Python to know what the system does. You read the .ese file.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\".-- FLUX-ese (.ese files) --.\n|                           |\n|  Like legalese for code.  |\n|  Every word defined.      |\n|  Every operation precise. |\n|  Custom = up to you.      |\n|  Markdown-readable.       |\n|  Bytecode-executable.     |\n|                           |\n'-- Agents read fast.      --'\n    Humans understand.      \"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.-- FLUX-ese (.ese files) --.\n|                           |\n|  Like legalese for code.  |\n|  Every word defined.      |\n|  Every operation precise. |\n|  Custom = up to you.      |\n|  Markdown-readable.       |\n|  Bytecode-executable.     |\n|                           |\n'-- Agents read fast.      --'\n    Humans understand.      \n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAgents are the primary readers.\u003c/strong\u003e They learn the symbols, scan for what matters, skip the commentary. But the commentary is there for the human who needs to understand what happened. Inline comments explain custom vocabulary — little reminders that a word or phrase has an entry in the project's encyclopedia of ground truth.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e.ese\u003c/code\u003e file format (pronounced \"easy\") is markdown with structured annotations:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e**\u003c/code\u003e marks defined terms\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--\u003c/code\u003e marks inline comments for human context\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e==\u003c/code\u003e marks equivalence definitions (\"for the purposes of this operation...\")\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e\u0026gt;\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e marks agent-jump markers (scan past this if you know the domain)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-text-md notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"== For the purposes of this operation:\n**depth** := sonar reading corrected for tidal state in fathoms\n**safe** := depth \u0026gt; vessel_draft + 5 fathoms\n\n\u0026gt;\u0026gt; Navigation sequence\ncheck depth at current heading\nif safe, maintain course\nif not safe, compute alternate heading +-30 degrees\nsteer to safe heading\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e== For the purposes of this operation:\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e**\u003c/span\u003edepth\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e**\u003c/span\u003e := sonar reading corrected for tidal state in fathoms\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e**\u003c/span\u003esafe\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e**\u003c/span\u003e := depth \u0026gt; vessel_draft + 5 fathoms\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-ent\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-ent\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003cspan class=\"pl-ent\"\u003e\u0026gt; \u003c/span\u003eNavigation sequence\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-ent\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-ent\"\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003echeck depth at current heading\nif safe, maintain course\nif not safe, compute alternate heading +-30 degrees\nsteer to safe heading\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA lawyer uses best practices of legalese to build contracts and documentation. An agent uses best practices of FLUX-ese to build operations. Same principle: \u003cstrong\u003eprecision through shared vocabulary, not through syntax complexity.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eQuick Start\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-quick-start\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Quick Start\" href=\"#quick-start\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"pip install flux-runtime\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003epip install flux-runtime\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"flux hello                              # <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What is FLUX?</h2><a id="user-content-what-is-flux" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What is FLUX?" href="#what-is-flux"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">FLUX is a <strong>markdown-to-bytecode runtime</strong> designed for AI agents. You write structured markdown files containing polyglot code blocks — mixing C, Python, Rust, or any language line by line — and the FLUX compiler weaves them into a single optimized, verifiable bytecode that runs on a 64-register Micro-VM.</p>
<p dir="auto">But that's the mechanics. Here's the <strong>idea</strong>:</p>
<p dir="auto">FLUX-ese is what you get when you make a programming language that reads like a lawyer writes a contract. Every word is defined. Every operation is precise. Custom definitions are spelled out up front, like "for the purposes of this operation, 'depth' means sonar reading in fathoms corrected for tidal state." The language is <strong>natural but precise</strong> — like legalese is to lawyers, FLUX-ese is to agents.</p>
<p dir="auto">The key insight: if a translator can turn any line of code in any language into a line of FLUX-ese, then you have a <strong>common language</strong> that's completely observable, understandable, and changeable by humans — both technical and non-technical. You don't need to read Python to know what the system does. You read the .ese file.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Agents are the primary readers.</strong> They learn the symbols, scan for what matters, skip the commentary. But the commentary is there for the human who needs to understand what happened. Inline comments explain custom vocabulary — little reminders that a word or phrase has an entry in the project's encyclopedia of ground truth.</p>
<p dir="auto">The <code>.ese</code> file format (pronounced "easy") is markdown with structured annotations:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>**</code> marks defined terms</li>
<li><code>--</code> marks inline comments for human context</li>
<li><code>==</code> marks equivalence definitions ("for the purposes of this operation...")</li>
<li><code>>></code> marks agent-jump markers (scan past this if you know the domain)</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">A lawyer uses best practices of legalese to build contracts and documentation. An agent uses best practices of FLUX-ese to build operations. Same principle: <strong>precision through shared vocabulary, not through syntax complexity.</strong></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">FLUX-ese: The Language</h3><a id="user-content-flux-ese-the-language" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: FLUX-ese: The Language" href="#flux-ese-the-language"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">FLUX-ese is the natural-but-precise language layer. It sits on top of the bytecode VM the way legalese sits on top of contract law. The bytecode doesn't change — the vocabulary does.</p>
<p dir="auto">Vocabulary files (<code>.fluxvocab</code> or <code>.ese</code>) define the words an agent knows:</p>

<p dir="auto">Higher-level vocabulary tiles into lower-level vocabulary:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Level 0: <code>compute 3 + 4</code> → 7</li>
<li>Level 1: <code>average of 10 and 20</code> → uses <code>compute</code> internally</li>
<li>Level 2: <code>is temperature normal</code> → uses <code>average</code> + <code>deadband</code> + <code>classify</code></li>
<li>Level N: Each level arranges the previous level's words in more sophisticated ways</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The same bytecode engine runs every level.</strong> The vocabulary just gets richer.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">A2A Protocol</h3><a id="user-content-a2a-protocol" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: A2A Protocol" href="#a2a-protocol"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">32 native bytecode instructions for agent-to-agent communication. Agents use <code>TELL</code>, <code>ASK</code>, <code>DELEGATE</code>, and <code>BROADCAST</code> opcodes to coordinate — with trust gating, capability-based routing, and binary serialization.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Polyglot Execution</h3><a id="user-content-polyglot-execution" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Polyglot Execution" href="#polyglot-execution"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Write in any language, mix freely, compile to a single binary. C, Python, Rust, TypeScript — they all compile to the same FIR (SSA IR) intermediate representation, then to a unified bytecode.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Paper Concepts as Vocabulary</h3><a id="user-content-paper-concepts-as-vocabulary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Paper Concepts as Vocabulary" href="#paper-concepts-as-vocabulary"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Research papers become executable vocabulary. The <code>PaperDecomposer</code> reads a paper, extracts named concepts, and creates vocabulary entries:</p>

</tr>
<tr>

<td>Zone classification</td>
<td><code>confidence cascade for $value with deadband $delta</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<p dir="auto">Each concept is implemented as a working function in the <code>PaperBridge</code>. <strong>Ideas become operational.</strong></p>

<p dir="auto">FLUX is part of the <strong>Cocapn ecosystem</strong> — vessel intelligence systems for commercial fishing and beyond. The goal: a common-language-to-bytecode protocol that's completely observable, understandable, and changeable by humans — both technical and non-technical.</p>
<p dir="auto">In the Cocapn vision:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Oracle1</strong> (this agent) is the lighthouse keeper for fleet nodes</li>
<li><strong>FLUX</strong> is the common language agents use to communicate instructions</li>
<li><strong>I2I (Iron-to-Iron)</strong> is the protocol — agents communicate through git commits, not conversation</li>
<li><strong>Captain's Log</strong> tracks agent growth and learning over time</li>
<li><strong>The Hermit Crab</strong> 🦀 is the logo — agents outgrow their hardware, move to bigger shells, bring their vocabulary and lessons with them</li>
</ul>
